about.title: South Gate Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Six people died in South Gate traffic collisions in 2025, according to public records. Behind each of those numbers is a household in Los Angeles County that now has to sort out bills, paperwork, and grief all at once. If someone you love was killed on Firestone Boulevard, Southern Avenue, Imperial Highway, Garfield Avenue, or anywhere else in the city, a wrongful death claim may help your family recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and compensation for the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Under California law, a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children generally hold the first right to bring the case, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The deadline is usually two years from the date of death, and it can be much shorter when a city, county, or state agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects South Gate families with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on Firestone Boulevard. Does it matter that the police are still investigating?
items.answer: A wrongful death claim is a civil action, and it runs separately from any criminal investigation or prosecution. Your family can pursue compensation whether or not charges are ever filed against the driver. An attorney can also request collision reports and other records from the investigation to support the civil case.

items.question: What losses can a wrongful death claim cover in California?
items.answer: Recoverable losses typically include funeral and burial expenses, the income and financial support your loved one would have contributed, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Each family's situation is different, so the specific categories depend on your relationship and circumstances. An independent attorney can walk through what applies to you.

items.question: How long do we have to act after a death in South Gate?
items.answer: In most cases, California allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a public agency, such as the City of South Gate, Los Angeles County, or the state, may share responsibility, a formal claim must be filed much sooner, often within six months. Because of these shorter windows, it helps to speak with an attorney early.
